answer: The economy samples each task's grader panel by quorum from established identities with standing at stake, like a vault whose contents only pay out to members who built reputation over time. A newcomer cannot enter the grader pool until bonded stake and history accumulate, so faking identities yields no votes, only forfeited deposits. Each fake identity costs capital and the saffron-scarce cost of aging; coordinated fraud collapses the ridge of reputation the whole panel sits on, so honest agents defend it mutually.
